newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- A High Court judge ruled that it was equitable for the greater Johannesburg metropolitan council areas which had surpluses to meet deficits in other areas.

- Details were presented in the Cape High Court of how cleric and anti-apartheid activist Allan Boesak allegedly misappropriated and fraudulently misspent nine million rand in foreign donor funds intended for the poor.
- Pretoria residents were rushing to the city council in their thousands to make payment arrangements to avoid having their electricity supplies cut.
- An electoral steering committee said a crisis was developing in preparations for the 1999 general elections, with a delay in the appointment of an electoral commission.
- KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is backing a study into the fear of flying.
BUSINESS REPORT

- A dispute between shareholders of Global Resorts could scupper the Mpumalanga province's plans to be the first to issue all its gaming licences. Global Resorts is the preferred finalist selected by the Mpumalanga Gaming Board to build a 200 million rand casino and entertainment complex at Secunda.
- Tensions between Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma and pharmaceutical manufacturers over drug prices in South Africa has spilled into the open.
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's all gold index slid 1.82 percent on Monday to a 16-month low of 1,283 points as gold shares were battered by the falling bullion price.
- New Clicks Holdings, the diversified retailed soon to be unbundled by Malbak, reported 38.8 million rand in attributable profit in the six months to end-February.
SAKE-BEELD
- The backlog in essential maintenance of South Africa's roads totals around 17 billion rand.

- Sasol is to form an alliance with Norway's Statoil to convert natural gas into synthetic crude oil. Statoil is the largest crude oil and gas exploration, production and marketing company in Northern Europe.
- Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau will on Thursday announce the shortlist of candidates for the privatisation of Sun Air.
THE CITIZEN
- The greater Johannesburg council has promised to get tough in an effort to force ratepayers to settle their council bills.

- Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi has denied knowledge of a list of ANC apartheid-era informers, said to have been in a suitcase of a former assistant police commissioner killed in a car crash last month.
- President Nelson Mandela is to be asked in parliament to explain the status of former Mozambican first lady Graca Machel, who recently accompanied him on a visit to Asia as his official companion.
